expectations.evidence: The rewrite adds "We've already got ideas for the next round of improvements" and "Build time still matters," which the original never states, and it changes "the engineer-hours we were losing" to "engineer time we recovered."
It uses an em dash as a connector in "$2,400 a month—far less than the engineer time we recovered" and opens with the punchy "Slow builds kill productivity."
Short concrete sentences like "Most of the time wasn't spent compiling. It was spent downloading the same dependencies over and over." mix with longer ones and read like an engineer wrote them.
It stays a plain engineering team blog post, with no hype, jokes, or bullet-list flattening, as in "We started by benchmarking all 11 services."
